Rank keyword phrases with RAKE degree/frequency scores

Source: R/rake_keywords.R
rake_keywords.Rd

Splits a single document at stopwords, punctuation and numeric tokens. Candidate phrases retain contiguous words (including internal apostrophes and hyphens). Word degree includes the word itself, so each occurrence in a phrase of length m contributes m. Phrase scores sum word degree/frequency. Repeated phrases are returned once, with an occurrence count; ties are sorted by phrase. This is the basic candidate-scoring procedure, without the optional adjoining-keyword postprocessing in Rose et al. (2010).

rake_keywords(text, stopwords, n_keywords = 10L)

Arguments

text

One non-missing character string.

stopwords

Character vector of word delimiters; specify a language- appropriate list, for example stopwords::stopwords("en").

n_keywords

Maximum positive integer number of phrases to return.

Value

A tibble with keyword, score and frequency columns.

References

Rose, S., Engel, D., Cramer, N. and Cowley, W. (2010). Automatic Keyword Extraction from Individual Documents. doi:10.1002/9780470689646.ch1 .

Examples

rake_keywords("red apple and red apple pie. apple", "and", 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   keyword       score frequency
#>   <chr>         <dbl>     <int>
#> 1 red apple pie   7.5         1
#> 2 red apple       4.5         1
#> 3 apple           2           1
